seo.title: Chapter 12 Export FAQ: Soybean Tariffs, Schedule B & Export Rules
seo.shortDescription: Common questions on exporting soybeans and other Chapter 12 goods, answered from the export tariff report.

intro: Common questions about exporting soybeans and other Chapter 12 goods, answered from the rest of this export report.
keyTakeaways: China is the only major buyer that taxes this chapter's goods — 10% on top of its normal rate — and its September 2026 goodwill list left soybeans out of the relief it gave other U.S. farm goods.
Every other top buyer — Mexico, Canada, the EU, Japan and Egypt — charges no tariff on this chapter's goods.
The U.S. side of exporting soybeans and grain is routine: a Schedule B number, buyer screening, FGIS inspection and weighing, and an AES filing; no export licence applies in the ordinary case.
questionSource: Google search suggestions for queries like "soybean export tariff", "china tariff on us soybeans", "schedule b code for soybeans", "export license soybeans", "do i need phytosanitary certificate soybeans".

faqs.question: Does China still tariff U.S. soybeans?
faqs.answer: Yes. On top of its 3% normal rate, China charges an extra 10% on U.S. soybeans and every other U.S. good, under the tariff fight that began in 2025. China's older, soybean-specific 25% retaliation tariff from 2018–19 is still on the books, but it is waived for soybeans through an exclusion process that currently runs to December 31, 2026, so soybeans effectively pay 3% plus 10%, not 3% plus 10% plus 25%.

faqs.question: Did China exclude soybeans from its 2026 tariff cuts?
faqs.answer: Yes. China's September 2026 goodwill list under the U.S.–China Board of Trade offered lower tariffs on corn, wheat, meat, dairy and other U.S. farm goods, but it explicitly left out non-seed soybeans — the single largest U.S. export in this chapter. The 10% tariff on soybeans stays in place.

faqs.question: What tariff does the EU charge on U.S. soybeans?
faqs.answer: None. The EU has applied a zero tariff on soybeans and soybean oilcake since a GATT commitment dating to the 1960s, one of the oldest trade concessions still in force for any U.S. export. That has not changed in the current tariff dispute.
searchedAs: does the eu tax soybean imports

faqs.question: Does Mexico charge a tariff on U.S. soybeans?
faqs.answer: No, as long as the shipment qualifies under USMCA — which almost all U.S. soybean exports to Mexico do. Mexico's own general (non-USMCA) tariff on soybeans runs 15–20%, but that rate does not apply to qualifying U.S. goods.

faqs.question: How much does the U.S. export in Chapter 12 (soybeans and oilseeds)?
faqs.answer: $21.36 billion in 2025, down 28.8% from 2024 as China pulled back sharply during the tariff fight. Soybeans alone are 77% of that total. Exports of this chapter were up 25% in the first seven months of 2026 as Chinese buying picked back up.
searchedAs: how much soybeans does the us export

faqs.question: Who buys the most U.S. soybeans?
faqs.answer: China and Mexico are the two largest buyers of this chapter's goods, together taking about 31% of 2025 exports, followed by Egypt, Japan and Indonesia. China's share fell sharply in 2025 as it bought more from Brazil and Argentina during the tariff dispute.
searchedAs: who buys the most us soybeans

faqs.question: What is the Schedule B code for soybeans?
faqs.answer: 1201.90.5000 for soybeans other than seed, the line behind almost all of this chapter's trade. Soybeans for seed use a different code (1201.10), and each of the chapter's other headings — seeds for sowing, hay and forage and the rest — has its own six-digit code matching the HS headings on the Overview page. Look up the exact 10-digit number with the Census Bureau's Schedule B search tool.

faqs.question: Do I need an export license to ship soybeans?
faqs.answer: No, in the ordinary case. Soybeans and almost everything else in this chapter are EAR99 — not on the Commerce Control List — so no Export Control Classification Number or licence applies. You still need to screen the buyer and destination, and a licence can be required for an embargoed country or a restricted end use.
searchedAs: do i need an export license for soybeans

faqs.question: Do I need a phytosanitary certificate to export soybeans or seeds?
faqs.answer: The U.S. does not require one to export bulk soybeans, but many buyers' plant-quarantine authorities do, and it is close to standard for seeds for sowing (1209) and for live or dried medicinal and herbal plants (1211). An APHIS-authorized certification official inspects the shipment and issues the certificate through the PCIT system.
searchedAs: do i need phytosanitary certificate for seeds

faqs.question: When does China's extra tariff on U.S. soybeans end?
faqs.answer: There is no announced end date for removing it. China's suspension of 24 of the 34 points of its original reciprocal tariff — which keeps the current rate at 10% instead of a much higher one — has been extended to January 10, 2027, with further talks expected before then. Separately, the waiver of the older 2018–19 retaliation tariff on soybeans runs through December 31, 2026.
searchedAs: when does china soybean tariff end
